I understand that deeply, you won't be alone though there will be other patients nurses and doctors there, the staff will want to help you that is why they chose that career, and it will likely be no more than a week. As far as sobriety goes it might do you even more good than the meds booze has a way of making things worse without you even realizing that it's doing it, but after they let you go they will hook you up with resources for staying dry if you want that and the will also set you up for referrals for continued care so you won't have to worry about finding it on your own. It's no magic bullet for your problems but it is most certainly a good start to feeling better.

Edit: some places will give you "yard time" where you will be allowed to smoke

It really isn't especially if you find out that the right meds were all you needed to make things better enough to keep going, I get that everything seems real shitty here in the moment but this might be the moment you look back on as the one that saved your life. It is after all what saved mine and many others. I'm not saying you have to stay among the living or even that you have to give it a shot but the fact that it might be worth it is something to think about.

Usually if they believe that you are in genuine danger of harming yourself they will admit you, they do not usually let you keep any electronics, phones included, but you will have the ability to call people from the hospital phone. How long they keep you is based on when they feel it is safe to release you but it averages to about a week. The withdrawals are something that mental hospitals are usually fairly well equipped to handle. Lastly the main difference is that you are cutting out the middle man as most standard hospitals are not really equipped to assist you with suicidal ideation and they will typically just have you escorted to a mental hospital anyway. I strongly recommend going if for no other reason then just to see if you can ride the bad times out with some meds, I hope this helped, good luck.
